monthly_review.summary: You've increased volume and intensity this month, with faster paces and higher HR across more demanding sessions — but at the cost of reduced time in foundational aerobic zones (Z1/Z2) and slightly elevated ground contact time.
monthly_review.highlight: Your Zone 3 time jumped from 19% to 29% while Zone 1+2 dropped from 79% to 54% — indicating a meaningful shift toward threshold work, but potentially at the expense of aerobic base resilience.

goal_tracker.message: You’ve already exceeded last month’s total distance by 5.5 km and need only one more run to match last month’s session count. No catch-up required — focus on quality over quantity for the remaining 7 days.

insights.title: Improved efficiency despite higher HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.42 to 13.62 m/sec per bpm, even as average HR increased +4 bpm — suggesting better cardiac output utilization or improved neuromuscular coordination at sub-threshold efforts.

insights.title: Sharp reduction in Z1/Z2 time
insights.body: Time in recovery (Z1) and easy aerobic (Z2) zones fell from 79% (36%+43%) last month to 54% (25%+29%) this month — a 25-point drop that risks under-recovery and limits mitochondrial adaptation.

insights.title: Cadence and stride length divergence
insights.body: Cadence increased +5 spm (146→151), yet stride length remained stable (~69 cm in long runs) and ground contact time rose slightly (314→317 ms in 11 km runs), suggesting compensatory tension rather than efficient power transfer.

insights.title: High-intensity exposure without Z5 progression
insights.body: Z4 time increased from 3% to 15%, yet Z5 remains minimal (2% this month, 0% last month) — indicating focused threshold work but no true VO2 max stimulus, which may limit ceiling development.

recommendations.action: Do one 45-minute Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) before June 28, keeping cadence ≥148 spm and ground contact <320 ms (per Garmin feedback).
recommendations.reason: To restore Z1/Z2 volume lost this month (down 25% vs last month) and support aerobic base resilience — especially given your recent avg HR increase and stable VO2 max (37–38).

recommendations.action: Perform one 6 km tempo run at Zone 3 HR (146–154 bpm), with first/last km at Zone 2 to buffer transition stress.
recommendations.reason: You spent 29% of time in Z3 this month (up from 19%), but your best pace (392 sec/km ≈ 6:32/km) suggests untapped threshold efficiency — this session targets sustainable Z3 neuromuscular patterning.

recommendations.action: Add two 3-minute barefoot strides post-run (on grass or track) focusing on light ground contact (<280 ms) and vertical oscillation <7.0 cm.
recommendations.reason: Your recent 3.0 km run showed optimal metrics (ground contact 274 ms, VO2 max 37.0, vertical osc 8.4 cm), but longer runs trended toward higher contact time (314–317 ms) — strides reinforce elastic recoil mechanics.

weekly_focus.description: Rebalance Z1/Z2 volume while sharpening Z3 execution — prioritize physiological recovery and neuromuscular precision over raw volume or speed.
